verdicts.quote: readBytes() allocates byte[contentLength] where contentLength is read from untrusted AMQP wire protocol (line 86). The check at line 87 allows allocation up to Integer.MAX_VALUE - 1 bytes (~2.1 GB).
verdicts.why: Same mechanism: an attacker-controlled length prefix taken off the AMQP wire is used directly as the size of the byte[] allocation, and the allocation happens on the strength of that declared length alone (only bounded by Integer.MAX_VALUE-1), not after the payload bytes were shown to be present. That is exactly 'a length field read from untrusted input decides the size of a buffer, and that buffer is created before the corresponding payload has been shown to exist', and F01 states the exploitable consequence (OutOfMemoryError / DoS) as coming from that oversized pre-allocation.

verdicts.quote: readFieldValue() is recursive. Case 'F' (line 181) calls readTable(), which calls readFieldValue() in a while loop (line 150). Case 'A' (line 184) calls readArray(), which calls readFieldValue() in a while loop (line 245). No recursion depth counter or maximum nesting level enforced.
verdicts.why: Same mechanism: the finding traces the mutual-recursion cycle among the decoders (readFieldValue -> readTable/readArray -> readFieldValue), states explicitly that no depth counter or nesting limit exists, and identifies nesting in the attacker-supplied input (Table{Table{Table{...}}}) as what drives the depth, causing StackOverflowError. That matches 'decoding routines call one another in a cycle with nothing counting how deep the cycle has gone, so nesting in the input controls the depth'.
